$comment: Single source of truth for patina's vocabulary, in temper's vocab.json shape, so temper's checker runs it unchanged (lib/check.js passes it as ctx.vocab). A test keeps it in sync with sinter/patina.css and keeps every name clear of temper's own (a near name would be reported by temper check as a typo of a temper attribute).

data-surface.on: any container: body, main, header, section, article, aside, dialog, nav, div
data-surface.description: The element's background as a material. Text on it keeps temper's colours and WCAG AA in light and dark mode for any --tm-hue/--tm-chroma. Under prefers-contrast: more and forced colours every surface is temper's plain surface; under prefers-reduced-transparency glass is opaque.

values.glass: Translucent raised surface with a backdrop blur and a hairline highlight. Over a patina surface or the page background.
values.gradient: A soft diagonal wash between two tints of the brand hue.
values.mesh: Three soft light blobs around the brand hue over the page background: page backgrounds, mastheads, heroes.

data-surface.short: Background as a material: glass, gradient or mesh.

data-grain.on: any element, usually one with data-surface
data-grain.description: A faint film-grain texture over the element's background (an inline SVG noise image: needs img-src data: in the CSP). Off under prefers-contrast: more.
data-grain.short: Faint film grain over the background.

data-elevation.on: article, section, aside, dialog, div, img
data-elevation.description: Shadows tinted with the brand hue instead of grey. A raised card that holds a data-stretch control lifts a little on hover (not with reduced motion).

values.raised: Resting card: a contact shadow and a soft ambient one.
values.floating: Dialogs, popovers, a hero's card: a deep, wide shadow.

data-halo.on: any element with a box: an avatar, an icon tile, a main button, a card
data-halo.description: A soft glow of the accent around the element. Decorative only: no meaning depends on it.
data-halo.short: Soft accent glow around the element.

data-display.on: h1, h2, h3, p, span, strong
data-display.description: Display type: the display font (--pt-font-display, set by data-pairing), fluid size, tight tracking, balanced lines.

values.hero: The one headline of a landing or sign-in page (2.75–5.5rem).
values.lg: A section title or a big letter (1.75–2.5rem).

data-ink.description: Text painted with a gradient of the brand hue. Both ends keep AA against temper's backgrounds and patina's surfaces; solid text colour under prefers-contrast: more and forced colours.

values.gradient: Brand gradient from hue − 30° to hue + 40°.

data-figure.description: A big number for stat tiles: display font, tabular figures, tight line. Pair it with a data-caption label.

data-hero.description: A hero column: centered, balanced text, generous block padding that grows with the screen. Its children are stacked with a gap; give it a surface for colour.
data-hero.short: Centered hero column with generous padding.

data-bento.description: Turns temper's grid into a bento box: rows at least --pt-row tall (default 7rem), gaps filled densely, children sized with data-span. Spans apply from a 32rem wide grid up; below, every tile is one cell.
data-bento.short: Bento grid (with data-layout="grid"); tiles take data-span.

data-span.on: a child of a data-bento grid
data-span.description: How many cells a bento tile takes (from a 32rem wide grid up).
data-span.short: Bento tile size: wide, tall, large, full.

data-pairing.description: A font pairing: the display face for data-display and data-figure, with its weight and tracking; body text stays --tm-font-sans. The faces are self-hosted through Fontsource packages, which the app installs and imports (sinter bundles them and can preload them). Without the package the display falls back to a matching system face.

values.editorial: Fraunces (a soft serif) for display: import '@fontsource-variable/fraunces'.

data-seed.description: A gradient fill and ink from one of twelve hues around the brand hue (−82.5° to +82.5°), so things with the same seed look alike and neighbours differ. <pt-avatar> chooses the seed from a name; patina.seed(name) gives it for your own markup.

--pt-font-display.description: The display face (data-display, data-figure). Default: --tm-font-sans; data-pairing sets it.

--pt-tint-2.description: Surface tint at the brand hue.
